newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: HORSE RACING-IRELAND'S TIMARIDA SET FOR CHAMPION STAKES.
newsitem.headline: HORSE RACING-IRELAND'S TIMARIDA SET FOR CHAMPION STAKES.

text.p: Top trainer John Oxx said on Thursday his Irish Champion Stakes winner Timarida, owned by the Aga Khan, will run in the English equivalent at Newmarket on Saturday.

"There was a bit of question mark about her earlier in the week (after a blood test showed signs of a bacterial infection) but she seems fine now and there is no reason to leave her at home," Oxx said.
"I think it will be the toughest race of her career with Halling and Bosra Sham in the field," added the Curragh-based handler.
Halling has a string of group one victories to his credit, while Bosra Sham won the 1,000 Guineas impressively before finding Mark of Esteem too good at Ascot last month.
Oxx said that he had not made a final decision on whether or not Timarida, winner of 10 races in five different countries over the last two years, would race again in 1997.
Saturday's betting: Evens Halling, 7-4 Bosra Sham, 5-1 Timarida, 10-1 Even Top, 12-1 First Island, 25-1 Glory of Dancer, 33-1 Tamayaz, 40-1 Wall Street.
